The last days before a winter festival in the poor quarter: dusk, heavy snow falling, a narrow lane between turf-roofed clay houses lit by tallow windows. In the foreground, inside a doorway, the midwife ALDA REED (see reference: grey shawl, linen cap) is writing on a NARROW SLATE (illegible marks only), about to turn it face-down; her free hand touches the little tin box at her bodice. In the lane outside, TARN (see reference) leads a COLLECTOR of the Warm Court through the snow toward a neighbour's house: the collector a tall figure in an ash-grey coat whose bare fingertips are the colour of skimmed milk gone off, carrying a slate and an iron tube wrapped in cloth. Neighbours watch from doorways holding up fingers, a number passed from fist to fist. Brooms lean by every door for the Last Day's sweeping. In a basket by the hearth inside, an infant with a red mark on his wrist lies beside two crusts of bread, one fresh and one cold.
